answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique FOIA request history flips the bet — requests filed and answered by agencies over years — and the horizon lands on the attacker instead. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the pulse compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the vault of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
